Commentary.Commentary: Their fielding was poor as we saw 4 catches being dropped which cost them dear. Stay tuned as we return after the innings break!
Pakistan got into the rhythm today with Riaz and Amir proving to be a threat, claiming 4 wickets each. Yasir Shah bowled tirelessly, kept the pressure on from one end and was rewarded with 2 wickets.

Warner and Renshaw gave Australia a good start with the latter completing his maiden Test half century. This set up beautifully for their middle order as the skipper, Smith and the youngster, Handscomb both completed their centuries taking the Aussies to a position of command. And, at the very end, a 49-run partnership for the last wicket saw Australia post a total in excess of 400.

Australia, on the other hand, would look to add some quick runs and take the total to as much as possible. Another interesting session coming your way in a short while. Stay tuned...

Smith and Handscomb added 35 more runs to their overnight stand before the skipper fell to Riaz. Once again he had a catch drop but this time couldn't capitalize on it. After that, started the Aussie fall as Maddinson, Wade and Starc fell in quick succession. Peter Handscomb, however, remained firm on the other end and completed his maiden Test century just before Tea!

Mohammad Amir followed him and he too, completed his 3-fer by picking up wickets of Wade and Starc. Yasir Shah once again continued from the other end, building up the pressure and could have had a couple of wickets to his name if not for drop catches.

The Pakistani fielders are out in the middle and are looking fresh. STEVEN SMITH and PETER HANDSCOMB will continue their innings and look to take Aussies to a big total. MOHAMMAD AMIR to begin the proceedings,

Pakistan didn't have a good day with the ball. Their lines and lengths weren't consistent especially with the first new ball and were suitably punished by the Aussie batters. Under the lights, with the second new ball they troubled the batsmen with getting it to move but to no avail. Can the Aussies bat the visitors out of the game? Or will the Pakistan bowlers come up with something special? Let's see what the day has in store for us...

Hello and a warm welcome to the Day 2 of the first Test between Australia and Pakistan. The hosts dominated Day 1 with a superb batting performance. Smith was once more at the heart of things as he remained unbeaten on 110 at the stumps. He got a couple of lives but he made sure that he makes most of them. He was supported well in the middle by the opener, Matthew Renshaw, who completed his maiden Test fifty and then by Peter Handscomb who is still out there with his skipper on 64.
...DAY 2, SESSION 1...

Pakistan would be happy that Mohammad Amir came back after he survived a major injury scare on his right knee and is looking in much better shape. The Pakistani seamers did make the ball talk with the second new ball but Rahat Ali was disappointing. Yasir Shah tried his best but the Aussie batsmen have countered him expertly. The unbroken stand between Smith and Handscomb is looking threatening. Will Pakistan script an inspirational fightback tomorrow afternoon or will the Aussies run away with the show? Join us at 0830 IST to catch all the action from Day 2. Till then, goodbye and take care!

After the first session, Smith and Renshaw stitched a crucial 76-run stand before the latter departed to a peach from Riaz. The Australian skipper carried on in a disciplined manner and rotated the strike along with the young Handscomb. Smith is a bit lucky to be out there as Sarfraz dropped a regulation catch and later, he edged a ball from Amir but strangely, there was no appeal from the Pakistanis. However, he has made the most of it by scoring a brilliant century and is looking hungry for more. Handscomb has got into his own and is looking set for a big one.

Another session for the Aussies. A terrific day for the home side as they have dominated the proceedings thoroughly and are poised to set a mammoth score on the board. The only period where the Pakistanis fought back was in the final hour of the first session. They took a couple of big wickets of Warner and Khawaja to claw back into the contest.

FOUR! GLORIOUS! Pitched outside off, Smith leans forward and drives elegantly through the mid off region for a boundary. He waits for the ball to reach the boundary and erupts in joy to celebrate his first century against Pakistan. He takes his helmet off and raises his arms in the air to celebrate.
Short and wide outside off, Smith gets in line of the ball to defend it.
Slinging across off, Handscomb lets that through to the keeper.
Back of length outside off, Handscomb stays back to defend it.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
Short and angling into the body, Peter stays in his crease to defend that straight into the ground.
A full length delivery outside off, Handscomb stays in line of the ball to defend it.
Pitched outside off, left alone.
Smith stays in line of the ball to defend it.
Swinging across, Peter finds an outside edge which falls wide and short of the fielder at third slip. They run a single in this process.
Angling into the stumps, Handscomb defends that really well.
Bit short outside off, left alone this time.
Pitched short and angling outside off, Peter goes fetching but he luckily does not find any contact there.
Angling into the stumps, Peter plays it really late to guide it towards the point fielder.
Good length delivery outside off, Smith lets that go through.
Outside off, Smith drives it towards mid off.
Pitched up, Smith drives it straight down the ground. That looked like it was going for a boundary but a brilliant stop from Misbah at mid off gave no runs away.

Into the stumps, Handscomb plays it from the back foot towards point.
Outside off, left alone.
Smith clips it towards the square leg region for a single.

Smith defends it from within the crease.
Back of a length delivery, Smith guides it towards backward point.

Slinging outside off, Peter guides it towards the gully fielder.
Angling into the stumps, Peter defends it showing the full face of the bat.
Full delivery on middle, Handscomb pushes it towards mid off.

Pitched up outside off, PH drives the ball towards the cover region and a misfield there results into a single.

Length delivery on the stumps, Handscomb camps back and defends it.
SECOND NEW BALL IS AVAILABLE NOW and it is taken straightaway. Meanwhile, MOHAMMAD AMIR comes back to bowl. He seems to be alright now.

FOUR! TOP SHOT! Dragged short by Yasir, Smith camps back and pulls it towards mid-wicket for a well placed boundary.

Shortish outside off, Smith cuts it towards backward point.

Handscomb reaches out to the line of the ball to defend it.

Smith camps back and punches square through off side for a single.
Smith drives it towards mid on.

2nd Fifty for Peter Handscomb in Test cricket.
Pitched outside off, Handscomb drives the ball through the cover region. The ball does not reach the fence but they run three of it. Handscomb has stuck it out really well.
Handscomb drags back to defend the ball.
Peter stays in his crease to defend it.
100-run partnership up for Smith and Handscomb.
FOUR! CHEEKY! Pitched up and outside off, Handscomb waits for it and just guides the ball towards the third man region for a boundary. 100-run partnership comes up for Smith and Peter.
Pitched outside off, Peter cuts it really late straight towards the gully fielder.
Smith drives the ball towards the covers region.
Smith gets in line of the ball to defend it.
Sliding into the pads, Peter flicks it onto the on side for a single.
Floated way outside off, Smith drives the ball between point and cover for a single.
Pitched outside off, Smith has played that towards point.
Floated up, Handscomb steps out of his line to guide it towards mid-wicket for a single.
Smith camps back to defend the ball.
Pitched outside off, left alone.
FOUR! SUPER SHOT! Pitched outside off, Smith stays in his place and drives it through covers for a boundary. Such a good shot.
MOHAMMAD AMIR is back onto the field.
FOUR! SUBLIME! Pitched up outside off, Smith gets in line of the ball and plays it straight down the ground for a boundary.
Into the stumps, Smith gets in line of the ball to defend it.
Angling into the stumps, Smith comes across to defend it off the line.
WAHAB RIAZ comes in for a bowl.
Time for Drinks.
Stays back to the length delivery and defends it nicely.
Drags his length back a bit, Smith camps back and works it to the leg side.
Tosses this one up on off, Smith comes forward and drives it back to Shah.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Tossed up around off, Smith drives it nicely past short cover for a couple. Moves to 80.
FOUR! LOVELY SHOT! Fullish delivery around leg stump, Smith whips it through mid-wicket and the ball races to the fence.
Length delivery on the stumps, Handscomb camps back and defends it down the track.
Fullish delivery outside off, pushed to the covers off the front foot.
Bowls a back of length ball on leg stump, Handscomb looks to pull it but misses and is struck on the thigh pad.
On a length angling across Handscomb. He taps it towards cover-point.
Bowls it straighter this time, Smith shuffles a bit and works it behind square for a run.
Back of a length delivery angling across Smith. He rises with the bounce and defends it.
Comes down the track to the loopy delivery and looks to hit it on the leg side but misses and takes it on his body.

Steps out again and defends it towards the bowler.
Bowls a full toss outside off, Handscomb steps out and eases it to deep mid off for a single.
Flighted delivery, Handscomb comes down the track and clips it wide of mid on for a single.

Fuller length ball this time, Smith drives it to mid on.
Straying on the pads, Handscomb clips it to mid-wicket for a single.
On a length on leg stump, Smith hangs back and tucks it behind square for a run.
Shortish delivery, Handscomb stays back and pulls it to the leg side for a run.
Shortish delivery outside off, Handscomb camps back and cuts it towards point where Shah makes a diving stop.
On a length outside off, Handscomb stays back and decides to leave it.
RAHAT ALI comes back for a bowl.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Smith dances down the track and defends it.
Loopy delivery outside off, spins away. Smith leaves it alone.
Tossed up around off, defended off the front foot to silly point.
Handscomb comes down the track and drives it towards Riaz at mid on. He gets quickly to the ball and hurls in a direct hit at the non striker's end but Handscomb was safely in.
Shortish delivery outside off, cut to the fielder at point.
Gets beaten by the slower one there. Changes his pace at 126.6 clicks and bowls it between middle and leg, Smith goes across and defends it in an unsual manner to the leg side.
Fuller length ball wide outside off, Smith reaches out to it and drives it to the covers.
Comes over the wicket and bowls a length delivery angling into Smith. He camps back and defends it back to the bowler stoutly.
On a length angling into Handscomb. He goes deep in his crease and works it through square leg for a single.

He is being carried off the field and that seems to be a really big blow for the Pakistanis. He is unable to walk even a bit and a stretcher comes in the ground to carry him out.

FOUR! WHACKED! Shortish delivery on middle and leg, Handscomb stands tall and pulls it hard towards backward square leg. Mohammad Amir comes running in to his left, slides to stop the boundary but gets his right knee stuck in the ground. The ball goes through him and rolls to the boundary. He is down on the ground, hope it is not that serious.
On a length on the stumps, Handscomb camps back and defends it to the off side.

Slow through the air outside off, driven hard to the man at short cover.

Quicker and shortish on off, Smith rocks back and punches it to the covers.

Tossed up on middle, defended solidly off the front foot.
Tossed up on middle and leg, worked behind square.
Tossed it up around off, spinning away. Smith comes forward to defend but gets an outside edge that lands in front of the diving Younis Khan at first slip.
Quicker one at 89 clicks on off, hurries on to Smith. He looks to pull it but gets an under edge onto his pads. That was a risky shot!
YASIR SHAH comes back into the attack.
Dug in short this time, Handscomb ducks under it and evades it.
WELL PLAYED IN THE END! Bowls a shortish delivery outside off, Handscomb rises with the bounce, rolls his wrists and taps it down as it lands in front of Shah at point.

FOUR! EXQUISITE! Fuller length ball wide outside off, Smith strides forward and caresses it through the covers and the ball whistles away to the boundary.
No ball! Digs this one short down the leg side, Smith ducks under it. He has also overstepped on this occasion in search of extra pace.
Bowls a length delivery outside off, coming in with the angle. Smith looks to pull his bat out at the last moment and gets a bottom edge to the slip cordon.
FOUR! DELIGHTFUL! Bowls a fullish delivery outside off, Smith uses his reach and creams it through the covers for a gorgeous boundary.
Quicker delivery outside off, Handscomb waits for it and late cuts it to the man at short third man.
Comes down the track, fetches it from outside off and whips it to the man at mid on.
Tossed up delivery, Peter dances down the track and pushes it back to the bowler.
Smith waits for it this time and nudges it behind square for a run.
Drags his length back this time, Peter hangs back and works it through mid-wicket for a run.
Loopy delivery around off, Handscomb strides forward and defends it nicely.
This time he lunges forward and defends it solidly.
Fuller length ball outside off, driven firmly to the covers but fails to find the gap.
On a length angling into Smith. He camps back and defends it.
Outside off, left alone.
Ian Gould has a word with Wahab Riaz and Misbah-ul Haq for running on the danger area.

Wide! Hurls this one way outside off, Smith has nothing to do with it. The umpire is obliged to call it a wide.

WAHAB RIAZ comes in for a bowl.
Again advances down the track and keeps it out.
Peter comes down the track and defends it nicely.
Tossed up on off, defended solidly off the front foot.

FOUR! 50-run partnership up for Handscomb and Smith. ASKING FOR TROUBLE AND GETS THE TREATMENT! Bowls a full toss outside off, Handscomb slices it behind point and the ball races to the fence. Great use of the feet and a good ploy to counter the spinners. 200 up for Australia.
He is again nimble on his feet as he whips the loopy ball but fails to beat mid on.
Comes down the track and eases it to the man at mid on.
Fuller length ball outside off, driven sweetly to short cover.
On a length on the stumps, Smith shuffles across in his usual fashion and defends it nicely.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Shortish delivery around off, Smith rises with the bounce and defends it down the track.

Comes down the track and defends it.

Fuller length ball this time on the stumps, angling away a bit. He comes forward and gets an outside edge towards the gully fielder who fumbles a bit. Two runs taken!

We are back for the final session. STEVEN SMITH and PETER HANDSCOMB will continue their innings. Will the skipper show the way for his young batsmen to handle the tricky night session or will the Pakistani bowlers outsmart them? RAHAT ALI will bowl the first over after Dinner. A fascinating final session of play awaits us!
...DAY 1, SESSION 3...

Pakistan will be really trying to come out sharp because the Aussie skipper looks in good shape for a big one. They might have got rid of him, had Sarfaraz pouched the catch just before Dinner. Now, they need to break this partnership which seems to be growing in order to get a look of their lower middle order. Batting under lights against the pink ball will be a big test for the hosts. Join us back in a while for the third session.

A decent session for the Australians where they saw Renshaw reach his maiden half century for the baggy greens. The southpaw and Smith were playing really well till Wahab Riaz got rid of Renshaw with a beauty. Smith has also marched towards his 19th Test fifty. The hosts look really commanding with the bat as no great threat has been posed by the Pakistani bowlers.
Handscomb advances down the track and eases the loopy delivery down to long off for a single. THAT WILL BE DINNER ON DAY 1!
Fullish delivery outside off, Handscomb lunges forward and drives it to the left of Misbah at short cover who does well to stop it.
Smith uses his feet and eases it through mid on for a single.

DROPPED! Bowls this one quicker on off, spins away venomously as Smith camps back to defend but seems to have missed it as the keeper fails to hold onto it. Ooh, however the replays spot a faint nick and Smith gets a retrieve. My colleague spotted the edge, need to have hawk like eyes to spot those. This could well prove to be a turning point in the match! He is the key man and you can't afford to drop him.

Stays back to the length delivery and defends it nicely.

Peter comes down the track and clips it wide of mid on for a couple.

Peter comes down the track and square cuts it to the point region.
Handscomb prods forward and defends it nicely.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Outside off, fifth leave in a row.
Bowls this one again wide outside off, an easy leave for Smith.
Wide outside off, left alone.

Tossed up on the stumps, eased to mid on for a brisk single.
FOUR! LOOSE DELIVERY AND IT GETS THE TREATMENT! Bowls a juicy full toss outside off, Smith leans forward and places it through backward point. Good timing on that one and the ball races to the fence.

On a length angling across Peter. He stands tall and pushes it towards cover-point.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Handscomb strides forward and defends it to the covers.

Length ball, Smith gets across and plays it through mid-wicket for a single.

We are back for the second session. Matthew Renshaw and Steven Smith will continue their innings. Can the young southpaw score his fifty and play a decisive knock? YASIR SHAH to start the proceedings with the ball after tea. It promises to be an exciting couple of hours of play. Here we go...
...DAY 1, SESSION 2...

The Pakistani bowlers did not use the new ball really well as they hardly troubled the openers. Yasir Shah also had a slow start but started building the tempo later on. The visitors would look to come out and strike after the short Tea break to have a go at the fragile middle order. Join us back in a while for the second session.

A mixed session for both the teams. Australia got off to a good start where both the openers played out the new ball really well. Warner and Renshaw both looked in good nick till the former shuffled way across to be adjudged LBW to Amir. Khawaja started off with a boundary but was soon sent back by Yasir Shah. Smith and Renshaw played it out till tea without any further damage.
Bowls the wrong 'un outside off and it spins away from Renshaw substantially after pitching. Renshaw comes forward and pushes at it but gets beaten! THAT'S TEA ON DAY 1!

Gives plenty of flight on this one and bowls it on the stumps, Renshaw stays leg side of the ball and looks to force it through the off side but gets an outside edge past first slip. Couple taken! Intelligent thinking from the leggie!

AZHAR ALI comes to bowl the final over before Tea. Can it prove to be an inspirational move?

Tossed up delivery, driven to the man at covers.

Shortish and outside off, cut to the man at point.

The players and the umpires come out in the middle. DAVID WARNER and MATT RENSHAW will open the batting for Australia. MOHAMMAD AMIR will start with the new ball. It promises to be an exciting first hour of play. Will the Pakistani seamers jolt the Aussie batsmen early or will they see through the new ball safely? Here we go...
AUSTRALIA win the toss and chose to bat. They are unchanged from their previous encounter. PAKISTAN have made two obvious changes as Misbah-ul-Haq and Yasir Shah come back into the side.

Hello and a warm welcome on Day 1 of the first Test between Australia and Pakistan in Brisbane. The hosts would be riding high on confidence after their emphatic victory against the Proteas in their previous Day/Night encounter in Adelaide. They have the momentum on their side and they would look to make it count. On the other hand, the Pakistanis would look to begin on a bright note after their disappointing show in New Zealand. Both sides have potent pace brigades and they would strive to make the ball talk. It would be a stern test for the batsmen. A humdinger of a contest awaits us and lets see which side comes out on top.
